# SwiftUI Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: a pattern library for building declarative, performant interfaces with modern SwiftUI on Apple platforms. Covers the Observation framework (@Observable with property-level tracking instead of the older ObservableObject, so only views reading a changed property re-render), a property-wrapper selection guide (@State, @Binding, @Bindable, @Environment and when each one earns its place), view composition (extracting small focused subviews to limit invalidation, reusable styling through ViewModifiers), type-safe navigation with NavigationStack and NavigationPath driven by an observable router, and render performance (lazy containers for large collections, stable identifiers in ForEach, keeping I/O out of body, Equatable conformance for expensive views). Includes #Preview recipes with inline mock data for fast iteration and a sharp anti-pattern list (async work in body or init, AnyView type erasure, creating view models in child views that do not own the data, ignoring Sendable). The emphasis is on judgment, not syntax: which pattern fits which situation. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; Swift and SwiftUI oriented throughout, so you need an Apple-platform codebase (iOS, macOS) to apply it. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
